description: MoinPDF uses LibreOfficeKit for one-shot conversion without also starting the soffice desktop application. Honor verbose=false, as the upstream Node converter does. Original corresponding source remains in MATBEE-SOURCES; these exact replacements are applied by scripts/prepare-office-assets.mjs.

replacements.description: PDF export does not use image page/part metadata. Match the upstream Node converter's direct load/save path and query editor parts only for actual image exports.

Start only LibreOfficeKit. Configure the synchronous conversion path before Emscripten constructs and caches the native environment: avoid nested background image import/scaling and formula-calculation tasks that can block the WASM runtime thread.
Honor the supplied verbose flag for LibreOffice stdout and stderr; no synthetic document contents are written to the browser console in normal use.
Keep warnings enabled without forcing all LibreOffice diagnostic categories.
Keep the diagnostic label consistent with the changed setting.

Let the outer browser Worker.terminate() stop the complete worker tree after document cleanup. Explicitly terminating pthread children immediately before their owner can strand native DedicatedWorker threads in Chromium; this also reproduces with a standalone nested-worker control on Chromium 140 and 156.

The destroy handler also delegates to the bundled LibreOfficeConverter.destroy(). Remove its separate pool and individual-child termination paths too, while preserving LibreOfficeKit cleanup and clearing the converter references. Only the outer owner terminates the worker tree after acknowledgment.
Pure load/save conversion does not post editor input events. Leave the regular LibreOfficeKit yield path enabled.
replacements.before: c.enableSyncEvents(),console.log("[LOK Worker] Enabled synchronous event dispatch (Unipoll mode)"),

replacements.description: Keep a single shutdown owner. After native document cleanup, acknowledge without scheduling self.close(); a concurrent self-close and page-side Worker.terminate() can strand Chromium threads. The page terminates the entire worker tree on acknowledgment, with a bounded fallback for an unresponsive runtime.
Do not enter synchronous LibreOfficeKit calls until all initial pthread workers have acknowledged their compiled module. Record the readiness barrier for the real-browser regression test.
replacements.after: {let p=self.PThread,w=[...p.unusedWorkers,...p.runningWorkers],t=Date.now();while(w.some(a=>!a.loaded)){if(Date.now()-t>10000)throw new Error("Office pthread initialization timeout");await new Promise(a=>setTimeout(a,10));}y({type:"progress",id:ge,progress:{phase:"thread-pool",percent:68,workers:w.length,readyWorkers:w.filter(a=>a.loaded).length}});}B("lok-init","Initializing LibreOfficeKit...");

replacements.description: Preallocate eight pthread workers before native calls; synchronous pthread startup cannot create new browser workers while its owner is blocked. Keep this pool bounded. Emscripten pthreads documentation: Special considerations.

Require an already loaded worker for synchronous native thread creation. Fail explicitly instead of dynamically creating an asynchronous worker and deadlocking. Record pool capacity for actual browser regression evidence.
replacements.after: getNewWorker(){var worker=PThread.unusedWorkers.pop();Module["onMoinPDFThreadStart"]?.({ready:worker?.loaded===true,unusedWorkers:PThread.unusedWorkers.length,runningWorkers:PThread.runningWorkers.length});if(!worker?.loaded)throw new Error("Office thread pool has no ready worker");return worker}
